Literacy Strategy Resource — Elementary Science

Strategy: Claim-Evidence-Reasoning (CER) Sentence Frames
Type: Writing
Instructional Purpose: Helps students organize observations into a scientific explanation by
separating a claim, the evidence that supports it, and the reasoning that connects evidence to claim.
Intended Student Behavior: After an investigation, students write one sentence stating a claim, one
or more sentences citing specific observed evidence, and one sentence explaining why that evidence
supports the claim, using provided sentence starters.
Teacher Role: Model one complete CER example using the class's own data before students write
independently; circulate to prompt students who conflate evidence and reasoning.
Appropriate Conditions: Best used after students have collected first-hand observational or
measurement data they can cite directly.
Typical Point of Use: Immediately after a hands-on investigation, before or in place of a purely
verbal wrap-up discussion.
Required Supports: A CER sentence-frame handout; a model example.
Conditions Where It Would Not Be Appropriate: Lessons with no investigation or data collection step,
or where time does not allow at least 8-10 minutes of independent writing.

Strategy: Think-Pair-Share with Vocabulary Prompt
Type: Vocabulary / Reading
Instructional Purpose: Reinforces correct use of new science vocabulary in context through structured
peer discussion before whole-class share-out.
Intended Student Behavior: Students first think silently about a prompt that requires using a target
vocabulary word, then discuss with a partner, then a few pairs share with the class.
Teacher Role: Pose a vocabulary-embedded discussion prompt, enforce individual think time, and select
which pairs share out.
Appropriate Conditions: Works well anywhere a lesson already has an open verbal discussion point.
Typical Point of Use: During hook or wrap-up discussion moments.
Required Supports: A displayed vocabulary-embedded prompt.
Conditions Where It Would Not Be Appropriate: Lessons where the existing discussion is already
tightly scaffolded and adding a formal protocol would slow pacing without adding literacy value.
